title: Dynamic Routing
summary: Select the appropriate agent or workflow from request intent, capability, authorization, and uncertainty while keeping routing decisions observable and reversible.
overview: Dynamic routing maps an incoming request to an execution path using information available at runtime. The destination may be a specialist agent, a deterministic workflow, a clarification step, or a human queue. Routing should separate eligibility from preference: policy determines which destinations are allowed, then quality and operational constraints determine which eligible destination is best.

A classifier's confidence is not a calibrated probability unless validated as one. Preserve an ambiguity route and evaluate routing against downstream task outcomes. A route that looks semantically plausible can still be wrong if the selected worker lacks the necessary tool, geography, or data entitlement.

production.poc: In a prototype, hand-labeled examples and a small rule table reveal the main intent boundaries before an LLM router is introduced.
production.production: Production requires a versioned capability registry, authorization filtering, calibrated acceptance thresholds, and a clear fallback for mixed intent. Log route reasons without exposing sensitive inputs.
production.scale: At scale, routing also accounts for regional availability, tenant policy, queue pressure, and cost. Avoid rapid route oscillation by using stable decision windows and recording the chosen policy version.

components.name: Request normalizer
components.role: Extracts language, product, tenant, channel, and explicit requested action.

components.name: Eligibility filter
components.role: Removes destinations that lack permissions, residency compatibility, or required capabilities.

components.name: Intent router
components.role: Ranks eligible destinations and identifies ambiguity or unsupported requests.

components.name: Capability registry
components.role: Publishes versioned worker contracts, supported intents, and operational availability.

components.name: Outcome feedback
components.role: Compares chosen routes with corrections, escalations, and actual task completion.

flow.title: Normalize request
flow.description: Preserve the original request while extracting trusted identity and business context separately.

flow.title: Filter destinations
flow.description: Apply tenant policy and capability requirements before any probabilistic classification result is considered.

flow.title: Classify intent
flow.description: Produce a structured route proposal with relevant evidence and an ambiguity indicator.

flow.title: Validate selection
flow.description: Confirm destination health and required tools; reject nonexistent or unauthorized route identifiers.

flow.title: Dispatch context
flow.description: Send the minimum required request packet with route and policy versions attached.

flow.title: Observe outcome
flow.description: Record corrections and unresolved cases for evaluation rather than automatically retraining on every user interaction.

useCase.title: Routing enterprise support requests
useCase.situation: A telecom provider receives requests combining account charges, connectivity outages, and service changes across several countries.
useCase.problem: Keyword routing sends an outage described as a billing problem to a team that cannot inspect network telemetry.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must identify the required capability and respect country-specific service access without losing mixed requests.
useCase.architecture: A policy filter constrains destinations, and a structured router selects billing, diagnostics, or a decomposition workflow.
runtime: An authenticated customer reports unexpected charges during an outage; the router recognizes two linked intents and creates bounded work for both.
The support interface shows the selected paths and allows a service analyst to correct routing with a recorded reason.
useCase.failure: When confidence is insufficient or a destination lacks required access, the request enters clarification rather than a random available worker.
useCase.impact: Track task completion by route, correction rate, ambiguity rate, and routing overhead. Overall accuracy can hide failures in rare high-impact intents.

tradeoffs.benefit: Handles varied language and contextual intent.
tradeoffs.cost: Adds inference cost and requires ongoing calibration.

tradeoffs.benefit: Enforces stable eligibility and common cases cheaply.
tradeoffs.cost: Growing rule sets can become difficult to maintain.

tradeoffs.benefit: Reduces queue delays when equivalent destinations exist.
tradeoffs.cost: Operational convenience must not override capability or policy.

failures.detection: Dispatch rejects the capability version or endpoint.
failures.recovery: Refresh the registry and select a compatible eligible route.

failures.scenario: Mixed intent is forced into one class
failures.detection: Repeated handoffs or unresolved subrequests appear in outcomes.
failures.recovery: Use decomposition or ask a targeted clarification.

mistakes.fix: Enforce access independently at the destination.
Include resolution quality, route cost, and escalation burden.

whenToUse: Requests genuinely require different capabilities or workflows.
Eligibility depends on tenant, geography, or authenticated context.
Ambiguity can be handled through clarification or review.
whenNotToUse: Every request uses the same tools and execution path.
Simple stable rules already achieve adequate routing quality.
No labeled outcomes exist to assess route correctness.
checklist: Version the capability registry and router policy.
Calibrate thresholds on rare important classes.
Track route corrections with reason codes.
